title: CLO 2025.1 - Patterns & Editor
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded to further enhance your work efficiency! In the new version, we have optimized alignment, animation, and other mode & editor-related functions. Watch the video to learn about the specific updates.
transcript:
This video introduces the updates related to modes and the editor.  
In the previous CLO version,  
when adding a project file, you could not select the desired color scheme directly from the open file.  
To change the color scheme, you had to do it in the color editor after opening the file.  
From the current version onward, when adding a project file,  
you can choose the color scheme you want to open.  
This function is very useful when you want to design a clothing style but also want to add a specific color scheme to the current project.  
Locate the file,  
add the project,  
open the desired project file,  
and in the popup window, a color option is added below the clothing.  
In the drop-down menu, select the color scheme to be added.  
You can choose all or customize it.  
Click the color button on the right to select the color scheme.  
This allows you to conveniently view the color scheme of each color.  
The color scheme for each color will be displayed as the fabric most used in the clothing.  
Please note that files created in version 2025.0 or earlier  
will only display the name of the color scheme, not the color scheme itself.  
If you choose "all,"  
the color schemes from both the file you added and the file you have added previously  
will be saved in the order of the project files.  
Click in the same order to combine them.  
Therefore, if you want them to match each other,  
the color scheme order and preservation are very important in both project files.  
Please note that if you want to add fewer color schemes  
to projects that already have more color schemes,  
the first color scheme will be used to fill the remaining color schemes.  
As usual,  
when you want to customize the color scheme,  
locate the file, add the project,  
open the desired project file,  
click the right button at the bottom of the clothing in the popup window,  
open the color list to select the color schemes you want to add,  
then the file will be combined according to the selected color schemes.  
For example, I have now selected the second and third colors of the swimsuit.  
After adding,  
they will be added as the first two color schemes of the current project.  
The first color scheme selected by the added project  
is color scheme 2 and black in this case,  
which will always be the combat suit,  
and will combine with the remaining color schemes in the current project.  
In the future, more options will be added  
to allow mixing and matching of color schemes from different projects.  
This update can help users improve work efficiency in color combination design.  
In the latest version of CLO,  
we have optimized the keyframe animation settings.  
The main improvements include  
color keyframe animation that supports twist materials,  
keyframe animation lighting in Vray rendering,  
and a new time-limited selection layer function.  
Open the color editor,  
add keyframes to each color animation column,  
then click play to preview the effect.  
You can see that the color keyframe is applied,  
and the color of the twist changes accordingly.  
This makes the animation transition more natural.  
Open the rendering window,  
go to lighting settings.  
You will notice that the light bulb icon has now been removed,  
but you can use the fire option as a replacement.  
After using the fire option, you can also set additional parameters.  
Users can add keyframes to each of the following settings,  
such as intensity, angle, color, width, height, etc.  
Here, a light bulb keyframe is added to the animation.  
Then set keyframes for the following options.  
You can control the strength and angle of different lighting stages in the animation.  
This can be used to adjust the light bulb effects.  
In addition, we have improved control over the circle size setting.  
After enabling this setting,  
you can also edit the radius, head shadow height, and ground mix settings.  
Each setting can have keyframes added.  
Finally, you can adjust the time range of the current animation.  
Click to the right on the animation layer.  
Select to limit the time range to the selected layer.  
You will see that the playback area adjusts to the selected layer range.  
Finally, choose to render the animation.  
You can obtain animations of twist color and lighting.  
We hope these updates improve your animation experience and simplify your workflow.  
In the previous version, projects in GLTF format were not supported for virtual model animation.  
Therefore, any joint animation applied to virtual models or animation based on storage would not be saved.  
Thank you for watching.  
In the new version, you can now choose to include virtual model animation.  
This optimization provides greater flexibility for animation processing.  
You can easily integrate virtual models into various platforms or workflows.  
Locate the file and select export GLTF 2.0 GLTF.  
In the window, select all virtual models.  
In the options below, select virtual model animation.  
Choose the animation type you want.  
If you want to preserve Google's structure for editing or playback in the future, this is an ideal choice.  
To bind Google's model, the best choice is to implement high-fidelity animation.  
You can flexibly choose the export settings most suitable for your project needs  
to obtain better-compatible files.  
Whether you focus on interactive experience or high-quality visual display,  
this function allows you greater freedom to create and perform virtual model animations.  
Thank you for watching.

chunks.content: ## Project File Color Scheme Selection in CLO 2025.1 This section explains the new feature in CLO 2025.1 allowing users to select color schemes directly when adding project files, improving workflow efficiency in clothing style and color design. In previous versions of CLO, when adding a project file, you could not choose a desired color scheme at the time of opening. Instead, color scheme changes had to be done later in the color editor. Starting with version 2025.1, users can select the color scheme immediately upon adding a project file. ### How to Use Color Scheme Selection - Locate and add the project file. - When opening the file, a popup window appears with a color option below the clothing preview. - Use the dropdown menu to select the color scheme to add. Options include selecting "All" or customizing specific color schemes. - Click the color button to view the fabric color most used in the clothing for each scheme. - Selecting "All" saves the color schemes from both the newly added file and previously added project files in the order they were added. - The order of color schemes is important for matching and preservation across project files. ### Important Notes and Limitations - Files created in version 2025.0 or earlier only display the name of the color scheme, not the actual scheme colors. - If adding fewer color schemes to a project that already has more, the first color scheme will fill the remaining slots. - To customize color schemes, open the project file, then use the popup window’s color list to select specific colors to add. - For example, selecting the second and third colors of a swimsuit will add those as the first two color schemes in the current project. - The first color scheme selected (e.g., color scheme 2 and black) will always be combined with the existing color schemes. - Future updates will allow more flexible mixing and matching of color schemes from different projects. This feature enhances workflow efficiency by simplifying color combination design directly when adding projects. --- ## Keyframe Animation Enhancements in CLO 2025.1 This section covers improvements to keyframe animation, including support for color keyframe animation on twist materials, enhanced lighting animation in V-Ray rendering, and a new time-limited selection layer function. ### Color Keyframe Animation for Twist Materials - Open the color editor. - Add keyframes to each color animation column. - Play the animation preview to see the effect. - The twist material’s color changes smoothly based on the keyframes, creating natural animation transitions. ### Lighting Keyframe Animation in V-Ray Rendering - Open the rendering window and go to lighting settings. - The light bulb icon has been removed and replaced with a fire option. - After selecting the fire option, users can set parameters such as intensity, angle, color, width, and height. - Keyframes can be added to these lighting parameters to animate changes over time.

chunks.content: - The twist material’s color changes smoothly based on the keyframes, creating natural animation transitions. ### Lighting Keyframe Animation in V-Ray Rendering - Open the rendering window and go to lighting settings. - The light bulb icon has been removed and replaced with a fire option. - After selecting the fire option, users can set parameters such as intensity, angle, color, width, and height. - Keyframes can be added to these lighting parameters to animate changes over time. - For example, the strength and angle of a light bulb effect can be controlled through keyframes. - Circle size settings now allow editing radius, head shadow height, and ground mix, each supporting keyframe animation. ### Time-Limited Selection Layer Function - Users can adjust the animation time range by right-clicking on an animation layer. - Selecting the option to limit the time range to the selected layer adjusts the playback area accordingly. - This allows focused editing and rendering of specific animation segments. ### Final Output - After setting keyframes and time ranges, users can render animations showing twist color changes and dynamic lighting. - These updates aim to improve animation quality and simplify the animation workflow. --- ## Virtual Model Animation and GLTF Export Improvements This section details new support for virtual model animation in GLTF exports, providing greater flexibility for integrating virtual models into various platforms and workflows. ### Previous Limitations - Earlier versions did not support saving joint animations or stored animations for virtual models in GLTF format. - As a result, animations applied to virtual models were not preserved upon export. ### New Features in CLO 2025.1 - Users can now include virtual model animations when exporting in GLTF 2.0 format. - To export: - Locate the file and select export as GLTF 2.0. - In the export window, select all virtual models. - Enable the option for virtual model animation. - Choose the desired animation type. ### Animation Type Options - Preserving Google's structure is recommended for editing or playback compatibility on Google platforms. - High-fidelity animation binding is ideal for achieving high-quality, realistic animations. - Export settings are flexible to accommodate project needs, whether for interactive experiences or high-quality visual displays. This enhancement allows users greater freedom in creating and performing virtual model animations, expanding integration options across platforms. --- # Summary CLO 2025.1 introduces significant improvements in project file color scheme management, keyframe animation capabilities, and virtual model animation export. Users benefit from direct color scheme selection when adding projects, advanced animation controls in both color and lighting, and enhanced GLTF export options that preserve virtual model animations, all contributing to a more efficient and versatile design and animation workflow.
